continuous gear kinematics.

svg.text: SERIES 1 • CARD 03 OF 10 • DOMAIN: KINEMATIC GEAR RATIOS & MODULAR ARITHMETIC • 12:1 EPICYCLIC REDUCTION • 15-MIN QUADRANT WEDGES
LESSON GUIDE: ELAPSED TIME & PLANETARY GEAR RATIOS
Grades 2–6 Elapsed Time & Modular Math • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

text.tspan: How far does the hour hand travel when
the minute hand turns one full circle
around the dial?
Rotate the minute hand to 6 (bottom of dial, 30 minutes).
Observe the internal gears: the hour hand advances smoothly
halfway between 3 and 4 (exactly 105° on the dial).
We need to add 45 minutes of elapsed time.
Insert three 15-minute wedges (3 × 15 min = 45 min).
Wedges cover 3 × 90° = 270° angular arc around dial.
Notice: The wedges bridge past the 12 o'clock mark!
3. ADVANCE MINUTE HAND: Turn hand clockwise across the 3 wedges past 4:00 to 4:15!
4. READ FINAL TIME: Hour hand at 4:15; minute hand at 3 (15 min).
Calculator Verification: Press Clock HMS Icon ([🕒] / [g][▸HMS] / [f][▸HR]) and run 3.30 [f] [▸HR] 0.45

g.text: CORE PRINCIPLE: TIME IS CONTINUOUS KINEMATIC RATIO

text.tspan: Digital clocks make students think hour hands jump instantly when minutes reach 60. The planetary
gears physically prove that time is a continuous ratio! Because 45 minutes is 3/4 of an hour,
the hour hand moves through exactly 3/4 of its 30° sector (22.5°), landing precisely at 4:15!
Set clock to 8:45. Add two 45-minute wedges (90 min). Where does the planetary gear place the
hour hand? (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)
